sections.title: Visual Pitch (§30M)
sections.md:
### Visual plan

The strongest picture for every line, picked from three (hooks from five). Scores out of 12: stop · line · feel · specific · fresh · makeable.

### Hook 1 — Thirty years. Thirty. Somebody get this woman a medal for putting up with me, right?

| | First frame | Stakes | Where | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **▶ picked** | the long table under the bulbs, thirty friends mid-laugh, Greg pushing up from his chair tapping his glass | a toast in front of everyone she knows — it's about to turn | the hosts' back yard at golden hour | 12/12 |
| B | close on Susan's face, the soft white cake between her and the lens, his voice off: 'You look like my mother' | the insult lands before we know who she is | the same table, tight | 11/12 |
| C | two friends at the drinks table whispering 'She did kind of stop trying' as Susan walks past | her friends have written her off | the drinks table by the deck | 11/12 |
| D | Susan at the mirror, the old foundation cracking grey in her smile line, the sponge stopping | the face he named, every morning | her bedroom dressing table | 10/12 |
| E | Paula crossing a lawn with both hands out: 'You look incredible, what are you doing?' | the woman she was compared to asking her | the same yard, months later | 10/12 |

### SC01 — the toast turns: warm and loud, then a quiet verdict landing on her still face in front of thirty friends

| Beat | Line | Picked | Route | Score | Also considered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SC01-SH01 | Thirty years. Thirty. Somebody get this woman a medal for putting up w | the whole long table under the bulbs, thirty friends mid-laugh, Greg pushing up from his chair tapping his glass | WORLD | 11/12 | LITERAL: a fork tapping a wine glass, close (7) · DETAIL: the uncut white anniversary cake among the candles (9) |
| SC01-SH02 | Thirty years. Thirty. Somebody get this woman a medal for putting up w | Greg standing low over the table, glass up, grin wide, the room laughing back at him | REACTION | 11/12 | LITERAL: Greg raising his glass (7) · WORLD: the guests' raised glasses filling the frame (8) |
| SC01-SH03 | Thirty years. Thirty. Somebody get this woman a medal for putting up w | Susan seated beside him, almost letting herself enjoy it, her glass lifting an inch | REACTION | 10/12 | DETAIL: her hand round the stem of her glass (8) · WORLD: a wide of glasses going up all down the table (7) |
| SC01-SH04 ★ hero | …thirty years. And I look at you lately and I just, I don't know. / You look like my mother, Susan. When did that happen? | close on Susan through the soft white cake, pushing in as his words land — her face the only thing that moves, and it doesn't | STAKES | 12/12 | REACTION: Greg's face as he says it (9) · WORLD: the table hearing it, forks stopping (8) |
| SC01-SH05 | Greg. Sit down. | her profile, turned up to him, two words low: 'Greg. Sit down.' | REACTION | 11/12 | LITERAL: her hand on his sleeve (6) · DETAIL: her jaw tightening, extreme close (8) |
| SC01-SH06 | Paula's the same age as you. Exact same. Look at her, then look at you | Paula from above, staring at her plate as his hand points across at her — named in front of everyone | STAKES | 12/12 | REACTION: the guests turning to look at Paula (6) · LITERAL: Greg pointing at Paula (8) |
| SC01-SH07 | Paula's the same age as you. Exact same. Look at her, then look at you | back on Susan, held too long, one breath, eyes level | REACTION | 11/12 | SYMBOL: her napkin crumpling in her lap (9) · WORLD: the table frozen around her (7) |
| SC01-SH08 | (no line — Greg drops back into his chair and reaches past the cake for) | high behind her: Greg drops into his chair, reaches past the cake for his drink, thirty people not moving | WORLD | 11/12 | LITERAL: Greg sitting down (7) · DETAIL: his hand around the drink (7) |
| SC01-SH09 | (no line — nothing moves; the bulb light flickers faintly on the white ) | the untouched anniversary cake, a fork resting beside it, the title landing | SYMBOL | 11/12 | WORLD: the whole silent table (6) · DETAIL: a candle guttering (7) |

### SC02 — the deeper cut: her friends' quiet verdict, said behind her back as she keeps walking

| Beat | Line | Picked | Route | Score | Also considered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SC02-SH01 | (no line — Susan stands, folds her napkin once and sets it beside the c) | her hands folding the napkin once and laying it beside the cake | DETAIL | 11/12 | LITERAL: Susan standing up (7) · WORLD: the table watching her stand (7) |
| SC02-SH02 ★ hero | …that was awful of him. | two friends in profile at the drinks table, heads together, Susan passing soft behind them mid-step | STAKES | 12/12 | LITERAL: two women whispering (8) · REACTION: Susan's ear catching it (8) |
| SC02-SH03 | …I mean, though. She did kind of stop trying. It's just sad to watch. | her face walking toward us, eyes flicking once, never breaking stride | REACTION | 11/12 | STAKES: her feet not slowing on the grass (9) · WORLD: the party going on behind her (6) |
| SC02-SH04 | (no line — Susan climbs the three deck steps, opens the glass-paned bac) | low from the lawn: she climbs the three deck steps and the door clicks shut on the party | WORLD | 11/12 | SYMBOL: the door closing, the glass showing the lights (9) · LITERAL: Susan walking inside (6) |

| Beat | Line | Picked | Route | Score | Also considered |

| SC03-SH02 | He humiliated me in front of everyone we know. But that wasn't the par | half her face in shadow, eyes opening on nothing — they'd already decided | REACTION | 11/12 | DETAIL: her fingers pressed flat against the door (10) · STAKES: the party laughter faintly through the glass (6) |

### SC05 — a friend concedes the truth, then does her face with her own hands — white, then her own skin

| Beat | Line | Picked | Route | Score | Also considered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SC05-SH01 | There's a thing Saturday. Whole group. You're coming. | Beth walking straight in without knocking, garment bag on her shoulder, Susan on the end of the bed | WORLD | 11/12 | LITERAL: a door opening (7) · REACTION: Susan looking up (7) |
| SC05-SH02 | So everyone can compare me to Paula again? She looks ten years younger | Susan small on the end of the bed, saying it to her hands | REACTION | 11/12 | STAKES: a photo of Paula on her phone (6) · LITERAL: Susan sitting (6) |
| SC05-SH03 | Paula had Botox last month. Of course she looks like that. That's need | Beth laying the garment bag down while she says it plainly — the honest friend, not a salesperson | CONTRAST | 11/12 | LITERAL: a syringe (8) · SYMBOL: a clinic receipt (8) |
| SC05-SH04 | I'm not saying you go do that. You don't need to. Come sit. Watch this | Beth pulling the stool out with one hand and nodding her to it | REACTION | 11/12 | LITERAL: a stool (5) · WORLD: the bedroom (6) |
| SC05-SH05 | Everything you've been wearing was built for a thirty year old, so it  | Beth tilting her chin to the window, the violet stick coming out under her palm like a secret, cap off | PRODUCT | 12/12 | LITERAL: the stick on the table (7) · DETAIL: the cap coming off (8) |
| SC05-SH06 | Everything you've been wearing was built for a thirty year old, so it  | macro in profile: the balm draws one white stripe up her cheekbone | PRODUCT | 12/12 | LITERAL: a white swatch on skin (8) · REACTION: Susan flinching at the white (8) |
| SC05-SH07 ★ hero | It reads your skin and becomes your exact shade. The niacinamide takes | one continuous take: the brush circles and behind it the white turns to her own skin, every line still there | PROOF | 12/12 | MECHANISM: pigment diagram (6) · CONTRAST: split screen before/after (7) |
| SC05-SH08 | It won't erase a wrinkle, no. Nothing does, not even what Paula paid f | Beth stepping back behind her, the mirror showing the evened cheek next to the other | CONTRAST | 11/12 | LITERAL: Beth talking (6) · PROOF: a magnified wrinkle unchanged (9) |
| SC05-SH09 | It won't erase a wrinkle, no. Nothing does, not even what Paula paid f | in the mirror, Susan leaning an inch in, looking at her cheek — evened, real, lines still there | PROOF | 11/12 | REACTION: her hand touching her cheek (8) · LITERAL: a mirror (6) |
| SC05-SH10 | …and this is all you did? | low and close: quiet disbelief turning to Beth | REACTION | 11/12 | DETAIL: her eyes in the mirror (8) · LITERAL: Susan asking (6) |
| SC05-SH11 | This is all I did. | Beth's one nod, plain | REACTION | 11/12 | PRODUCT: the stick in Beth's hand (7) · LITERAL: Beth answering (6) |

### SC06 — the mirror, her enemy all film, gives her back

| Beat | Line | Picked | Route | Score | Also considered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SC06-SH01 ★ hero | …there she is. | her eyes holding her own in the mirror, not flinching for the first time | REACTION | 12/12 | SYMBOL: the mirror light (7) · LITERAL: Susan at the mirror (6) |
| SC06-SH02 | She never left. You just needed one person who didn't believe them. | over her shoulder: Beth's hand on her shoulder in the reflection, the two of them in the glass | CONTRAST | 11/12 | REACTION: Beth's face (7) · LITERAL: two women in a bedroom (6) |

### SC07 — the same yard: the group that saw her fall sees her come back, and Paula asks her

| Beat | Line | Picked | Route | Score | Also considered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SC07-SH01 | Saturday. The same yard I'd been hiding from for months. I almost turn | across the street: her car at the curb, engine off, white balloons on the mailbox, nobody getting out | WORLD | 12/12 | LITERAL: a car parking (7) · SYMBOL: the balloons (7) |
| SC07-SH02 | Saturday. The same yard I'd been hiding from for months. I almost turn | through the driver's window: her hands tight on the wheel, Beth's hand on her arm, one breath out | REACTION | 12/12 | LITERAL: keys in the ignition (7) · STAKES: the party seen through the windshield (7) |
| SC07-SH03 | (no line — Susan and Beth walk in from the side of the house onto the l) | the same table, the same lights: heads turning, the talk stopping, then Friend A lighting up | CONTRAST | 12/12 | WORLD: the party in full swing (6) · LITERAL: Susan arriving (7) |
| SC07-SH04 | Susan. Look at you. You look incredible, what are you doing? | Paula crossing the lawn to her first, both hands out | PROOF | 12/12 | REACTION: Paula's surprised face (7) · LITERAL: two women hugging (6) |
| SC07-SH05 ★ hero | Funny. Greg told me to come ask you. | Susan, easy, the corner of her mouth lifting as she says it | REACTION | 12/12 | CONTRAST: Greg in the background (7) · LITERAL: Susan talking (6) |
| SC07-SH06 | (no line — Paula catches it, a surprised breath, then a real laugh, the) | the two women laughing in profile; far behind, Greg small and going still | CONTRAST | 12/12 | REACTION: Greg's face alone (8) · WORLD: the party laughing (6) |
| SC07-SH07 | (no line — a knife cuts a slice from the white sheet cake and a hand pa) | the same cake shot: now a knife cuts a slice and a hand passes the plate along | SYMBOL | 11/12 | WORLD: people eating cake (6) · LITERAL: a slice of cake (6) |

| SC08-SH04 | I didn't get younger. I didn't take him back. I never gave up. I just  | high wide, the rhyme of the frozen table: Susan in the middle of her friends under the bulbs, Greg alone at the edge | CONTRAST | 11/12 | WORLD: the party at dusk (7) · LITERAL: Greg standing (7) |
